items.q: Explain double entry.
items.a: Every transaction has two equal effects: a debit and a credit in different accounts, so the accounting equation stays balanced.

items.q: What is the difference between a journal and a ledger?
items.a: The journal records transactions in order of date; the ledger groups them by account.

items.q: How do you do a bank reconciliation?
items.a: Start with the bank and book balances, list outstanding cheques, deposits in transit, charges and interest, adjust, and confirm both agree.

items.q: What is input tax credit?
items.a: The GST paid on eligible business purchases that can be set off against output GST, subject to conditions.

items.q: What do you do when the trial balance doesn't tally?
items.a: Find the difference, check divisibility by 9, review recent vouchers and one-sided entries, and fix at source without plugging.

steps.title: Structure
steps.body: Use STAR for stories: Situation, Task, Action, Result. Keep answers around 60–90 seconds.

steps.title: Language
steps.body: BPO rounds often include a voice and grammar screen; speak slowly and clearly, and avoid fillers.

steps.title: Never badmouth
steps.body: Criticising a previous employer or teacher marks you as a risk.

activity.prompt: Practise out loud. Read each model answer and then say your own version.

items.q: Tell me about yourself.
items.a: Give four lines: current status, one strength, one relevant skill, why this role. 'I'm a commerce graduate, patient with people, comfortable typing at 40 wpm, and I want a career in customer support.'

items.q: Why customer support?
items.a: I enjoy solving problems for people and communicating clearly; support gives quick feedback and a path to team lead, quality or trainer roles.

items.q: How do you handle an angry customer?
items.a: I listen without interrupting, apologise for the experience, verify details, take ownership and give a clear next step with a timeline. I stay calm and don't take it personally.

items.q: Are you comfortable with night shifts?
items.a: Answer honestly. Say yes only if you have considered the schedule and travel.

items.q: What if you don't know the answer?
items.a: I say 'Let me check that for you', search the knowledge base, ask a senior if needed and call back if promised.

items.q: Where do you see yourself in three years?
items.a: Growing into a senior agent or quality analyst, building domain skills and helping new joiners.
